samples.verdict_basis: An unsigned DLL with no exports autonomously starts an IPC key-recovery worker on DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH, obtains Chromium protected-key plaintext using browser elevation-service COM interfaces, and returns it to an external pipe peer. Its private CookiveV2 build provenance and malware-corpus collection support hostile use; no authorized importer or assessment deployment is evidenced. Standard MSVC dependencies and an asInvoker manifest do not neutralize this purpose.
execution_trace: Entry 0x180009b08 -> CRT dispatch 0x1800099e0 -> DllMain 0x180005b70. On process attach, DisableThreadLibraryCalls; CreateThread at 0x180005b98 starts 0x180005340; CloseHandle closes only the thread handle.

Worker initializes COM STA at 0x180005391. GetCurrentProcessId at 0x1800053a4 feeds four XOR/rotate transforms (A5A5A5A5/3C6EF372/1BF5A7E1/9E3779B9), formatted with %08X%08X%08X%08X and prefixed with the local named-pipe namespace. This derives an IPC identifier, not payload encryption.

WaitNamedPipeA at 0x1800056aa waits 5000ms. CreateFileA at 0x1800056e6 opens the pipe for GENERIC_READ|GENERIC_WRITE with OPEN_EXISTING. 0x180002010 reads a four-byte length then a ciphertext vector; 0x1800049b0 reads the browser selector with PeekNamedPipe/ReadFile.

0x180004790 case-folds the supplied selector and looks up browser configuration. It falls back to 0x180003d00, which gets the current host image path and selects Chrome, Chrome Beta, Brave, Edge, or Avast, otherwise throwing Unsupported host process. This is not an unconditional host check when a recognized selector is supplied.

Configuration builder 0x180002210 constructs paths and CLSIDs/IIDs with four immediate DWORD stores. IElevatorChrome GUID at 0x1800023dc..0x180002403 is split across four MOV instructions; an IElevator2 GUID follows. GUIDs are ordinary structured constants, not sufficient evidence of malicious obfuscation.

0x180004d00 wraps input bytes as BSTR using OLEAUT32 ordinal 150 (SysAllocStringByteLen). Chrome/Brave dispatch through 0x1800073a0, Edge through 0x180007200, Avast direct. CoCreateInstance uses CLSCTX_LOCAL_SERVER=4. CoSetProxyBlanket uses packet privacy=6, impersonate=3 and dynamic cloaking=0x40; this configures security rather than disabling it.

COM virtual calls at vtable offsets 0x28, 0x40 or 0x68 recover plaintext according to the selected interface; errors produce DecryptData failed. The returned BSTR byte length uses OLEAUT32 ordinal 149 (SysStringByteLen), empty keys are rejected, data is copied, and ordinal 6 frees the BSTRs.

Worker calls 0x180005100 to format each plaintext byte as two hexadecimal characters, then WriteFile at 0x180005821 writes the result to the same pipe. Scope is local IPC key export, with no established remote destination.

IsDebuggerPresent at 0x18000a164 belongs to MSVC failure reporting; TerminateProcess at 0x180009bf5 terminates the current process on runtime failure. Neither establishes analyst evasion or victim process killing.

limitations: No supplied injector/controller, delivery chain, or authorized deployment context. Do not claim this DLL injects itself, steals SQLite cookies, persists, downloads payloads, or sends data over the network.

Two distinct hostile results are supported: browser-key recovery and export to the IPC peer. These remain below the requested 3–5 goal because additional attacker objectives were not found after entry/worker/COM/protocol/CRT/section/TLS tracing; adding another would duplicate these or invent behavior.

Existing BSTR import rules match API names, while filefacts emits unresolved OLEAUT32 ordinals 149/150/6. No ordinal-only rule was added because the matcher cannot bind those numeric imports to a library, risking false API attribution. Observed key recovery is covered through the COM/GUID/diagnostic chain instead.
ML remains BENIGN at level -1 despite two hostile rules; probability moves from 0.769279 to 0.820256. This is a classifier miss, not a reason to restore a misleading suspicious brand-table feature.

The native hex-output formatter is traced at 0x180005100, but neither setw(2) nor a digit loop alone binds the output to hexadecimal. No unsupported generic hex-encoding claim was added from those primitives.
